solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Is he used to getting drunk in pubs?

indicators.note: someone drunk is all over the place, so the four words before this are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether a certain man is accustomed to drinking heavily in bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' rearranges ISHEUSEDTO. TIED HOUSES are British pubs bound to sell one brewery's beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tied house is a British public house contracted to sell only one brewery's beers.

clue.text: Promote right in Conservative city of old

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, and in a down entry the letter for right climbs higher in the word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A call to advance a right-winger within the Conservative Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' gives R, which 'Promote' lifts one place up inside TORY; in a down light, up means earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad, besieged by the Greeks.

clue.text: Scope to lower boom in a storm

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so these two words' letters are thrown into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A sailor needs space to lower the boom on a yacht in heavy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is space to move freely, which is what scope means here.

clue.text: Establishment providing spicy egg and lettuce starters

parts.note: spicy food is hot

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the words egg and lettuce

explanation.surface: A restaurant serving a spiced egg and lettuce dish as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like a menu course, but it takes the first letters, E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a business establishment offering lodging and meals.

clue.text: The oily manner required for topless work

indicators.note: topless means the word for work loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: a function is a job or work done

explanation.surface: An odd remark that greasy flattery is needed for a topless job.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction can mean an excessively smooth, ingratiating manner, an oily kind of charm.

clue.text: Free range case of eggs makes you angry

indicators.note: freed letters are let loose to settle in a different order
the case of a word is its outer letters, here the first and last of eggs

explanation.surface: Discovering that a box of free-range eggs is something else annoys you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges RANGE plus ES, the outside of 'eggs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrages is a direct synonym of infuriates, making someone very angry.

clue.text: Express disapproval bearing gift

parts.note: to boo is to express disapproval
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Someone jeers while carrying a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a welcome benefit or blessing, something granted like a gift.

clue.text: Some mothers-to-be see themselves as such!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pregnant women may regard themselves as rather large.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: 'as such' points back to the hidden word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pregnant women may jokingly see themselves as very fat, which is what this describes.

clue.text: Head merely starts encouraging a football skill

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

indicators.note: starts takes only the opening letter of merely

parts.note: egging, as in egging on, means encouraging

explanation.surface: A coach says heading the ball merely starts to encourage good play.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmegging is playing the ball through an opponent's legs, a football trick.

clue.text: Place in cockpit for parachutes — worry!

parts.note: to parachute is to jump from an aircraft
to eat at someone is to worry them

explanation.surface: A nervous flyer frets about the parachutes beside their cockpit seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump seat is a folding extra seat in a cockpit, used by an observer.

clue.text: Gold coin in America in circulation

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a bit is an old American coin value, two bits making a quarter

explanation.surface: A gold coin moving around in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a circular path, so circulation here is going round.

clue.text: Fat Charlie gets rich importing rubies originally

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: importing means bringing something in, so a letter goes inside the word for rich

parts.note: opulent means rich

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of rubies

explanation.surface: A plump man named Charlie becomes wealthy by bringing in gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word joining Charlie to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent is a formal synonym of fat, describing a large body.

clue.text: Burgeoning retail activity taking in women

indicators.note: taking in means one word swallows a letter inside itself

parts.note: selling is what retail does

explanation.surface: Shops are booming because they are attracting more female customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Swelling means growing or expanding, a synonym of burgeoning.

clue.text: In America, one shoots a man on board

definitions.meaning: in American slang a gun is called this

explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor, but it is a chess piece; the first sense is US slang for a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a handgun in US slang and a chessman.

clue.text: Badly copied rail publication

indicators.note: something badly done is messed up, so the letters of the next two words are mixed

explanation.surface: A poorly reproduced railway magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical is a magazine or journal published at regular intervals.

clue.text: Feeling generated by English movement

parts.note: motion means movement

explanation.surface: A sentiment stirred by an English cultural movement.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling such as joy or anger.

clue.text: Mentioning changes without me singing

indicators.note: changes says the letters of mentioning are rearranged, with those of me set aside

explanation.surface: Someone mentions that things change when they are not singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' tells you to take ME out of MENTIONING; 'changes' rearranges the rest, NTIONING.
explanation.definitionFit: Intoning is chanting or reciting in a singing tone, as in church.

clue.text: Preparing food in a state of mental turmoil

definitions.meaning: slowly simmering meat and vegetables in liquid

definitions.text: in a state of mental turmoil
definitions.meaning: fretting anxiously, as in being in a stew

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cooking slowly in liquid and brooding anxiously.

clue.text: Comprehensive girl ultimately trapped by involving us in vice

indicators.note: trapped by means a letter is caught inside the scrambled group
involving, in its sense of entangling or twisting together, mixes the letters of us in vice
ultimately points to the last letter of girl

explanation.surface: A girl ends up caught by a scheme drawing everyone into wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' rearranges USINVICE; 'trapped by' sets L, from 'ultimately', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclusive means taking everything in, so it is a synonym of comprehensive.

clue.text: People locked up at home with friends

parts.note: in means at home
mates are friends

explanation.surface: Housebound people stuck indoors with their pals.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmates are prisoners, people confined in a jail.

clue.text: A bit of a result — a natural leader's wife!

indicators.note: a bit of says the answer is a piece taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A partial victory proves that the boss's wife is a born leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is the wife of a sultan, a Muslim ruler.

clue.text: I may hide in ruined vacant buildings in Rome

indicators.note: may hide in means a letter tucks itself inside the scrambled word
ruined means wrecked, so the letters of vacant are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone might take shelter in derelict empty buildings in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges VACANT; 'may hide in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the papal palace and buildings in Rome, the seat of the Pope.

clue.text: A sour disposition and rising anger after French wine

indicators.note: after places the anger piece behind the wine piece

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: rising, in a down entry, means the word for anger reads upwards

parts.note: rage is anger

explanation.surface: Someone sour-tempered grows angrier after drinking French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar can mean sourness of character, an acid, ill-tempered disposition.

clue.text: Senior member's swindle with foreign currency

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: An elder of the club has run a scam involving foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of member's means 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or longest-serving member of a group.

clue.text: Positive response protects a source of revenue for ages

indicators.note: protects means the outer word shields the other letters inside it

parts.note: yes is a positive response

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of revenue

explanation.surface: A yes vote safeguards one income stream for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Years and ages both mean a very long time.

clue.text: Name included in record catch from journey

indicators.note: included in places a letter inside the word for record

parts.note: a log is a record
a haul is a catch, of fish for instance

explanation.surface: A fisherman logs his named catch at the end of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A long haul is a long-distance journey, especially a flight.

clue.text: Lofty-sounding doctor — a monster!

indicators.note: sounding says the word for lofty is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: high means lofty

explanation.surface: A high-and-mighty doctor turns out to be a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' turns HIGH into HY, said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra is the many-headed serpent monster of Greek myth.

clue.text: Beheading puts an end to troubles

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, the first letter, of the word for puts an end to

parts.note: kills means puts an end to

explanation.surface: Executing people by decapitation ends their problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are troubles or misfortunes.

clue.text: Joined Labour party

parts.note: read not as signing up to the political party but as a group of convicts linked together and set to hard work

explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour party' suggests the British political party; read literally it is a working party, joined by chains.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang of convicts chained together while doing hard labour.

clue.text: Military exercise? It bores

definitions.meaning: soldiers' marching practice on the parade ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both parade-ground training and a hole-boring tool.

clue.text: Hapless son comes into fortune

indicators.note: comes into means the letter for son goes inside the word for fortune

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune

explanation.surface: An unlucky son inherits a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost can mean helpless or hopeless, as in a lost cause, so hapless.

clue.text: They help in church, dears, with early changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of dears and early are rearranged

explanation.surface: Church helpers are told, my dears, that the early service has moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay readers are non-clergy licensed to lead parts of church services.
